summary: Tracks 2D blobs from point data, usually tx/ty Cartesian scan channels, and can output blob centroids, velocity, and persistent tracking information.
key_concepts: Consumes 2D Cartesian point data, normally tx and ty channels, and groups nearby points into persistent blobs.
Hokuyo and Leuze radial scanner data should be supplied in Cartesian coordinate mode before Blob Track can analyze it correctly.
All-points search is more robust for unordered point clouds, while Consecutive Points is faster when neighboring spatial points are adjacent in samples.
Area of Interest can restrict tracking to off/rectangle/circle regions, with center, size, rotation, and outside-movement behavior controlling persistence.
Output Centroid, Output Velocity, initialization time, lost timeout, and prediction mode govern whether blobs become stable tracked targets.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Enable blob tracking without clearing existing blobs when off

key_params.name: maxblobs
key_params.note: Maximum number of blobs to track

key_params.name: maxpointdistance
key_params.note: Maximum distance for points to belong to the same blob

key_params.name: maxblobmovement
key_params.note: Maximum frame-to-frame movement for preserving blob identity

key_params.name: areaofinterest
key_params.note: Optional rectangular or circular tracking region

key_params.name: center
key_params.note: Center of the area of interest

key_params.name: size
key_params.note: Size of the area of interest

key_params.name: rotate
key_params.note: Rotation of the area of interest

key_params.name: allowmovementoutside
key_params.note: Keep blobs tracked after they leave the area of interest

key_params.name: minblobpoints
key_params.note: Minimum points required to accept a blob

key_params.name: blobinittime
key_params.note: Time before a new blob is considered trustworthy

key_params.name: lostblobtimeout
key_params.note: Time before an occluded or lost blob is removed

key_params.name: predicttype
key_params.note: Off, simple forward prediction, or Kalman prediction

common_gotchas: Input channels should be named tx and ty and represent 2D Cartesian positions.
Consecutive Points mode is faster, but only works when nearby spatial points are adjacent in CHOP samples.
All mode is more robust for unordered points but can be slower on large scans.
Area of interest and movement limits can silently drop fast-moving blobs if they are too tight.
Hokuyo and Leuze-style radial scans should be converted to Cartesian coordinates before tracking.
